#### [!] K1.race RE-CHARACTERISED (2026-10-10): it is NOT cross-role and NOT `mixed`-only

Three arms, 12 runs each, same build and seed:

| arm | FA2 role blocks | FA2 work | failures |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fa3` @ `SM_SPLIT=128` | present | none | **0 / 12** |
| `mixed` @ `SM_SPLIT=128` | present | yes | 1 / 12 |
| `fa3` @ `SM_SPLIT=all` | **none** | none | **1 / 12** |

`fa3` with **no FA2-role blocks at all** fails at the same rate as `mixed`. All three rates are
within sampling noise of ~1/12, so FA2 co-residency is irrelevant.

**RETRACTED:** every earlier statement that this race is "`mixed` only", "the co-resident
configuration", or "a cross-ROLE hazard on the partial slab the FA3 epilogue shares with Runner1's
persistent params". That came from small samples -- `fa3` @ all had passed 5/5 and then 8/8, and I
treated two clean runs of 8 as evidence of absence for a 1-in-12 event. **At p = 1/12, eight
passes have probability 0.50** -- the sample never distinguished the arms.

**What is actually implicated:** the FA3 split path, independent of FA2. Consistent with the other
measurement I have on it -- parallelising `store_partial`'s O write across all MMA threads took the
rate from 1/10 to 8/10, which is in exactly this code. And `FUSED_NOSPLIT=1` has never failed,
though that needs its own repeat count before it counts as evidence (the error I just made).

**Sized experiment RUN (2026-10-10), `MODE=fa3` @ `SM_SPLIT=all`, 35 runs per arm:**

| arm | failures / 35 |
|---|---|
| `FUSED_NOSPLIT=1` (no partials, no merge) | **0 / 35** |
| splits on (16 chunks) | **3 / 35** (8.6%), rel 0.41 / 0.51 / 0.60, 1 bad row each |

**Stated honestly, because this is the trap I just retracted: 0/35 vs 3/35 is SUGGESTIVE, NOT
CONCLUSIVE.** Fisher's exact gives **p ~ 0.24**, and the 95% upper bound on 0/35 is ~8.2%, which
overlaps the split arm's 8.6%. Thirty-five runs was enough to distinguish 1/12 from 0 but the
split arm's true rate is lower than assumed, so the arms barely separate. A conclusive no-split
arm needs ~100 runs (0/100 bounds the rate at 3%).

**What makes the split path the target anyway is INDEPENDENT evidence, not this comparison:**
parallelising `store_partial`'s O write across all MMA threads took the failure rate from 1/10 to
**8/10**, and that is split-path code. Two unrelated observations pointing at the same region is
worth more here than one underpowered A/B.

**[x] ROW INDEX RECORDED (2026-10-10), and it is a Q-TILE BOUNDARY every time.**

Added bad-row indices to the harness (`BADROWS`). Failing rows observed:

| fixture | failing row | token | q tile |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mixed` | 0 (repeatedly) | 0 | tile 0, first row |
| `fa3` | **128** | 128 | tile 4, first row |

At G=4 a q tile spans 128 packed rows = **32 tokens**, so tokens 0 and 128 are both the **FIRST
row of a q tile**. The location is deterministic, the occurrence is not -- which rules out a
general memory race and points at one specific work item.

**Mechanism this suggests, and it is specific:** the first row of a q tile has the SMALLEST causal
bound in that tile (bottom-right causal: fewer keys the earlier the token). So it is the row that
can have **zero valid keys within a given kv chunk** while later rows of the same tile still have
some. `get_num_kv_tiles` is computed from the tile's LAST row, so the item runs and
`store_partial` writes **all** rows of the tile -- including a row whose online-softmax state is
degenerate: `m = -inf`, `d = 0`, so O is `0/0` and LSE is `-inf`.

The merge then computes `scale = exp2(other_m - m)`. With both `-inf` that is `exp2(NaN)`, and
`0 * garbage` or `NaN * 0` propagates depending on what the other chunks contributed -- which is
exactly a defect whose *presence* is deterministic but whose *visible effect* depends on values
and ordering. It also explains why the observed rel varies so widely (0.04 to 0.80) for a single
bad row.

Note this is adjacent to, but NOT the same as, the fully-masked-chunk bug already fixed: that one
was a chunk where the item was skipped entirely (`num_kv_tiles <= 0`) and never wrote its slot.
This is a chunk where the item RUNS but one of its rows has no valid keys.

**[!] HYPOTHESIS REFUTED by reading the whole slab (2026-10-10).** A degenerate-state scan over
all 115584 partial slots, run 6 times:

```
slots=115584  nonfinite_LSE=3584  nonfinite_O_rows=0  min_lse=-0.0319
slot=105 merge_row=0 (tile_row=0) chunk=15 head=0 lse=-inf   [same 6/6 runs]
```

- **`nonfinite_O_rows = 0`: O is ALWAYS finite.** So no `0/0` ever reaches the slab and the
  degenerate-NaN mechanism proposed above is **wrong**.
- The 3584 `-inf` LSE entries sit at **chunk 15** (the last chunk) for the early rows, i.e. exactly
  the chunks beyond those rows' causal bound. `-inf` paired with `O = 0` is the CORRECT merge
  identity there, and it is what `store_partial_zero` is supposed to write. So this is the fix
  working, not a bug.
- The count and the slot list are **identical across all 6 runs**, so the non-finite pattern is
  deterministic.

**What this redirects to.** The partial *values* look correct and their degenerate pattern is
deterministic, yet the OUTPUT varies run to run. So the nondeterminism is either (a) in the
reduction's combination of those partials, or (b) in some partial slot whose value differs between
runs without being non-finite -- which this scan would not catch, since it only tested finiteness.

**[x] ROOT CAUSE LOCALISED (2026-10-10): `partial_o` is NONDETERMINISTIC while `partial_lse` is
NOT. The race is the `sO` / `smem_v` union, on the O side only.**

Slab fingerprint across runs (`MODE=fa3` @ `SM_SPLIT=all`, same seed, same build):

```
lse_sum = 768993.500000   lse_absmax = 7.005718   n_finite_lse = 112000   <- IDENTICAL every run
o_sum   = 1467.978 / 1468.258 / 1468.412                                  <- DIFFERS every run
```

So the attention grid is **deterministic in its softmax statistics and nondeterministic in its O
accumulator as written to the slab**. That asymmetry is the whole diagnosis:

- `partial_lse` is written **straight from registers** (`lse(mi)` out of the updater) -> stable.
- `partial_o` is written **from `sO` in shared memory**, and `sO` is **unioned with `smem_v`**
  (`union { smem_v; smem_o; }` in the SharedStorage). `smem_v` is exactly what the producer warps
  refill for the next work item.

**Everything previously measured now fits one mechanism.** The single-warp gate on the O write is
load-bearing because it keeps the `sO` read window short; parallelising it across all
`NUM_MMA_THREADS` widened that window and took the failure rate from 1/10 to **8/10**. One warp
makes the window small enough that the race lands ~1 in 12.

**And this is where `tma_store_wait` belongs** -- the goal names it, and `store_tail()` in our
epilogue is `{ // tma_store_wait<0>(); }`, i.e. **commented out**. 0.7's `store()` writes O by TMA
and relies on that wait to guarantee the store has drained before `sO`/`smem_v` is reused. Our
`store_partial` writes with plain vectorised stores and has **no completion handshake at all**, so
nothing orders the producer's next V load against the consumer's `sO` read.

**[!] CORRECTION (2026-10-10): the "offset 0" fix I proposed LAST TURN WAS ALREADY TRIED, and
the recorded results about it CONTRADICT EACH OTHER. It must be re-measured, not implemented.**

It already exists as a compile flag -- `FLASHINFER_FUSED_ALIAS_SMEM` makes
`fused_pers_smem_base()` return 0, otherwise it returns FA3's size rounded to 1 KB. So aliasing
FA2's storage onto FA3's is a one-flag change that has been in the tree all along, and the comment
block above it carries **two measured claims that cannot both be true**:

1. *"Now DISJOINT BY DEFAULT, because symmetric mode's FA3 output is wrong nondeterministically
   (rel err 1.93 / 2.53 / 3.31 across identical runs, one run exact) and only when a CTA drains FA2
   before entering FA3. A CUTLASS warp-specialised kernel initialises its pipeline mbarriers in
   shared memory at entry, **before the sm_split branch**, and with a base of 0 the drain's slot and
   its cursor/merge tail at ~69648 land inside FA3's 98352-byte SharedStorage."*
2. *"MEASURED, and it does not work: with FA3 at one stage so that it fits, **the disjoint layout
   fails 2 configurations on every run (0 clean in 10), while the same 1-stage FA3 with shared
   memory REUSED is clean 14 times in 14**."*

(1) says aliasing races; (2) says aliasing is clean 14/14 and *disjoint* is the broken one. They
are from different sittings and were never reconciled.

**And (1) names a real obstacle to my proposal that my reasoning missed.** I argued "a block is
one role, never both, so the layouts can alias". That is false for the mbarrier initialisation:
CUTLASS initialises FA3's pipeline mbarriers at **kernel entry, before** the `sm_split` branch, so
**every** block -- FA2-role included -- writes into FA3's region at offset 0 regardless of the role
it goes on to take. Aliasing therefore is not obviously safe, and my "with numbers" confidence last
turn was unwarranted.

**So the next step is a measurement, not an implementation:** build with
`FLASHINFER_FUSED_ALIAS_SMEM` at `STAGES=2` and run `mixed` @ `SM_SPLIT=128` x 35 against the
current disjoint `STAGES=1` baseline (1/10). That settles (1) vs (2) on today's tree, where both
were recorded before several of today's fixes landed. Only then is it worth changing the layout.

**Method note, since this is the third time today:** I proposed a fix whose prior attempt was
already recorded in the file I was editing. Grepping for the mechanism (`fused_pers_smem_base`,
`ALIAS_SMEM`) before designing the change would have surfaced it immediately -- cheaper than
designing it and cheaper than implementing it.

**[!] REFRAMING + A FAILED FIX ATTEMPT (2026-10-10). `STAGES=1` was never a valid
configuration, and the obvious way to enable `STAGES=2` is wrong.**

**Reframing, which corrects my own wording above.** Stock 0.7 has the SAME `union { smem_v;
smem_o; }` -- but it runs **2 stages by default**, and double buffering is precisely what makes
that union safe: the producer's next V load targets the *other* stage, so it cannot overwrite the
`sO` the epilogue is still reading. Our port set `STAGES=1` to fit shared memory and thereby
**removed an invariant stock relies on**. So `STAGES=2` is not "a mitigation hiding a race" --
`STAGES=1` was an invalid configuration from the start.

**Failed attempt, recorded because the failure is the useful part.** The 69632 B reservation that
blocks `STAGES=2` is created by a block commented as the scheduler's "cluster slot", so I gated it
off on the reasoning that cross-role backfill (B2c) is unused. Result: **`mixed` 25 FAILURES / 25.**
The reservation is **not** a backfill queue -- it is where the **FA2 runners' SharedStorage lives**,
placed past FA3's region by `fused_pers_smem_base`. Gating it starved every FA2-role block of its
workspace. Reverted; revert verified back to **1 / 10** on `mixed`, i.e. the known race rate.

**What that failure establishes, as arithmetic:** in the co-resident configuration the allocation
must cover FA3's layout (any block may take the FA3 role) **plus** the FA2 region at an offset past
it -- `164864 + 69632 + 48 = 234544` against a `232448` B device max. **`STAGES=2` and co-residency
are incompatible with the CURRENT layout**, which is why the STAGES=2 result only holds at
`SM_SPLIT=all`.

**THE RIGHT FIX, identified with the numbers and not implemented:** FA2-role blocks should address
their storage from **offset 0**, not past FA3's. A block is either FA3-role or FA2-role, **never
both**, so the two layouts can safely **alias across roles** -- making
`smem_size = max(FA3, FA2) = 163920`, which fits with ~68 KB spare and lets `STAGES=2` launch
everywhere. The past-FA3 placement is only required when one block does both, which is exactly the
cross-role drain (B2c, unimplemented). So this change is a prerequisite for B2c as well, and it is
the smallest change that closes the race in the configuration that matters.

**[x] MECHANISM CONFIRMED BY A PREDICTED INTERVENTION (2026-10-10), and there is a viable
mitigation.** The diagnosis predicts that with `NUM_STAGES = 1` the producer's next V load targets
exactly the memory `sO` aliases, while with `NUM_STAGES = 2` it targets the other stage. Tested,
35 runs per arm, `MODE=fa3` @ `SM_SPLIT=all`:

| arm | failures / 35 | bad rows seen |
|---|---|---|
| `FA3_STAGES=2` | **0 / 35** | — |
| `FA3_STAGES=1` (control) | **3 / 35** | 224, 64, 96 |
| `FUSED_NOSPLIT=1` (earlier) | **0 / 35** | — |

**And the q-tile-boundary pattern now has six observations and holds every time:** bad rows 0, 64,
96, 128, 224 -- all multiples of 32, i.e. always the FIRST row of a q tile (a tile spans 32 tokens
at G=4).

**Evidence quality, stated plainly:** each 0/35 vs 3/35 comparison is individually weak (Fisher
p ~ 0.24). What carries this is that **three independent interventions all behave as one mechanism
predicts** -- removing the split (0/35), adding a V stage (0/35), and widening the `sO` read window
(1/10 -> 8/10) -- plus a deterministic failure location that the mechanism explains. That is a
different kind of evidence from one underpowered A/B, and it is why I am willing to name the cause
here when I was not willing to earlier.

**Mitigation available now: `FA3_STAGES=2`.** It is perf-neutral (0.2563 vs 0.2590 ms measured
earlier) and launches since the drain-slot gate fix. **Its limit, recorded rather than glossed:
STAGES=2 only launches when `fa2_can_run` is false (`sm_split == nsm`), so it does NOT cover
`mixed` at `SM_SPLIT=128` -- the co-resident case.** Covering that needs the drain slot shrunk from
`max(r1,r2,r3) = 69632` to the runner that actually drains (r2 = 32768), which buys the 2096 B the
launch is short.

**The real fix is still the missing store-completion handshake** -- a 2-stage pipeline hides the
race rather than ordering the accesses, and a 3+-chunk item could still wrap onto the aliased
stage. Options, unchanged: a named-barrier arrival after the global write that the producer waits
on, or route the partial O write through TMA and restore `tma_store_wait<0>()` in `store_tail()`.
The TMA route matches 0.7, makes the port upstreamable, is the same primitive B2c's cross-role
backfill needs, and would also unblock the 12% `store_partial` parallelisation that had to be
reverted.

#### B1 RESULT (2026-10-09): the headroom is real but it is mostly GEMM, not attention

Driver `drv/b1_headroom.sh`, analyzer `drv/b1_analyze.py`, trace
`/dev/shm/w/prof/1791522716.762536-TP-0.trace.json.gz` (355.7 MB). 4-mode MTP server, EAGLE3
chain draft (topk 1, 4 draft tokens), split ON / guard OFF / graphs off, warm pass before the
capture, load during it (`--random-input-len 2048 --random-output-len 128 --request-rate 24
--max-concurrency 48`). Composition during capture:
`FUSED_SPLIT_CALLS 501 (fa3_rows=2 fa2_rows=22 onesided=3)`, `MIXEDSPEC_STEPS 1`.

**66.5 ms of GPU time over 7250 launches.**

| role | launches | GPU ms | share of GPU time | small N (grid<132) | small share of role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **gemm** | 1538 | **52.16** | **78.5%** | 1446 | 88.4% |
| attention | 1595 | 7.68 | **11.6%** | 1225 | 87.5% |
| epilogue/elementwise | 3637 | 5.93 | **8.9%** | 3612 | 98.4% |
| memcpy/memset | 468 | 0.68 | 1.0% | 468 | 100.0% |
| other | 12 | 0.02 | 0.0% | 12 | 100.0% |

**89.3% of GPU time is in launches that cannot fill the device** (6763/7250 launches, 59.37 of
66.49 ms, grid < 132 blocks). Top kernels are `nvjet_sm90_*` (cuBLASLt) at median grid 100-112 --
the TARGET model's own linear layers failing to fill 132 SMs at this batch size.

**What this means for the two main items, stated against the bar:**

* **Item A (tile dispatcher) is bounded by 11.6%** of GPU time, and item **B (epilogue fusion) by
  8.9%** -- about **20% combined, before** discounting the part that is not actually reclaimable
  (a fused kernel still has to do the arithmetic; only the idle-SM fraction is recoverable).
* So **no attention-side work can reach the >=30% TTFT/ITL target**, which is consistent with the
  independent `g * a * 0.18` arithmetic recorded earlier that put the ceiling at ~5-7%. Two
  different measurements now agree on that conclusion.
* **The dominant idle capacity is GEMM**, at 78.5% of GPU time with 88.4% of it in
  sub-132-block launches. If the paper's kernel contribution is to be proportionate to the
  motivation table, it has to touch that -- e.g. cross-role backfill at the GEMM level (draft
  model GEMMs filling the SMs the target's GEMMs leave idle), which is a different and larger
  piece of work than the attention split.

**The honest reviewer-facing framing**, which this table supports and the previous framing did
not: *in colocated spec-decode serving the GPU is chronically underfilled -- 89% of GPU time in
launches that cannot occupy the device -- and fusing across roles is how that capacity is
reclaimed.* Attention is the demonstrator, not the whole prize, and the table says so.

**Caveat on scope, recorded rather than buried:** `MIXEDSPEC_STEPS 1` against 501 split calls
means this capture is dominated by ORDINARY extend batches, not 4-mode merges -- with the guard
off and paged forced, the split fires on any two-sided extend batch. A 4-mode-heavy capture could
shift the attention share up somewhat. It will not change the GEMM dominance, which is per-token
work, but the exact A/B bounds above should be re-read from a capture where
`MIXEDSPEC_STEPS` is large.

      | `PersistentKernelTemplate<BlockBatchPagedAttentionPersistent...>` (`BatchAttention`'s) | **12.49%** | 2 / 2 | 1.00 |

      **Our kernel is pinned to ONE block per SM by registers AND shared memory at once.** 18.75%
      of peak warps is exactly our 384-thread block (12 of 64 warps) with a single block resident,
      and dec=128 gives the identical 18.75%. So there is no room to co-schedule anything *within*
      an SM: the role split is strictly spatial ACROSS SMs and never overlapped inside one. That is
      structural, not a tuning artifact.

      **And the reference runs at LOWER occupancy -- 12.49% -- while being 3.14x FASTER.** So
      achieved occupancy does not predict performance on this workload, and the motivation "the GPU
      is underfilled, therefore fuse the small kernels" does not survive its own measurement. B1b
      already cut that claim from 89.3% to 8.1% of GPU time; B1e removes the warp-fill version of
      it as well.

      Driver `/dev/shm/w/occ2.sh`. **Method note:** the first attempt profiled EVERY kernel in the
      process and reported `softmax_warp_forward` at 9183 invocations, `arange` and
      `CatArrayBatchedCopy` -- the harness's own fp32 REFERENCE path, not the kernel. It spent 11
      minutes at 1% GPU and its numbers must not be read as kernel occupancy. Filtered to
      `-k regex:(Fused|Persistent|persistent)` with `--launch-count 24`.

      Launch geometry is the weaker claim and B1e above now supersedes it with the measured

#### B1d RESULT (2026-10-09): item A is priced, and its value depends on the MTP config

`sglang-up@ed6eef498` adds host-side FLOP-weighted tile-coverage accounting
(`mixed_dispatch.tile_waste_accumulate` / `tile_waste_report`, `SGLANG_FUSED_TILE_STATS=1`).
Per row it charges `ceil(packed_qo/width)*width x ceil(kv/TILE_KV)*TILE_KV` covered against
`packed_qo x kv` useful, bucketed by `packed_qo`. No profiler and no timing: the waste item A
targets is a property of the SHAPES, and grid-level occupancy structurally cannot see it (a
48-row item in a 128-wide tile keeps every SM busy while most of each tile idles).

**A metric bug caught before it produced a wrong conclusion.** The first version charged
`TILE_Q = 128` to every row and reported **88% waste** on packed-16 verify rows. That is
invented headroom: those rows route to FA2's existing **`tile16`**. Fixed to charge each row its
ACTUAL width -- FA3 always 128; FA2 its class (128 above 64, else 64 above 16, else 16).

**Verify-dominated steps** (no large prefill row to dilute the FLOPs), 48 rows, kv 2000:

| config | `packed_qo` | charged tile | waste |
|---|---|---|---|
| GQA 4, 4 draft tokens -- **our current config** | 16 | 16 | **2.3%** |
| GQA 7, 8 draft tokens | 56 | 64 | **14.6%** |
| GQA 12, 4 draft tokens | 48 | 64 | **26.8%** |
| GQA 7, 12 draft tokens | 84 | 128 | **35.9%** |

**Mixed steps** (one 2048-token prefill chunk + verify rows): overall waste collapses to
**0.3% - 2.1%**, because the prefill row carries **89-94% of useful FLOPs at zero waste**
(packed 8192 is exactly 64 tiles of 128).

**Verdict on item A, stated plainly:**

1. **At our current config it is worth essentially nothing** -- 2.3% of attention FLOPs in the
   best case for it (verify-only), 0.3% in a realistic mixed step. Attention is 20.5% of GPU
   time, so that is under 0.5% end-to-end, far below the **+/-1.5-3%** noise floor.
2. **At other MTP configs it is worth a great deal** -- up to **35.9%** of attention FLOPs. The
   pattern is sharp: waste is large exactly when `packed_qo` lands just above an available
   width, and FA2's widths are only {16, 64, 128}.
3. **The decode-population guard already prevents the specific waste originally suspected.**
   `split_classes` returned `fa3_rows=1` in every mixed case: rows in the 48-127 band are
   un-routed from FA3's fixed 128-wide tile to FA2, where they get 64. So A1 (dynamic 128/64 in
   FA3) addresses a case the guard mostly already avoids.
4. **The worst remaining band is 65-128**, not 16-64. Packed 84 charged 128 wastes 35.9%; the
   proposed width set {16,32,48,64} does not cover it. **`tile96` would pay more than `tile32`.**
5. **Item A's value is therefore a function of `num_draft_tokens x gqa`, which is a spec-config
   choice, not something the kernel controls.** If the kernel contribution is to matter, the
   config has to put `packed_qo` in an awkward band -- and more draft tokens is independently
   desirable for acceptance length, so this is a coherent design direction rather than a
   contrivance. But it must be stated as a config-dependent result, not a general speedup.

- [x] **B1d DONE: item A priced.** 0.3-2.3% at our config; 14.6-35.9% at GQA 7-12 with 8-12
      draft tokens in verify-dominated steps.
- [ ] **A2 revised: instantiate {16, 32, 48, 64, 96} and measure**, with `tile96` prioritised --
      the 65-128 band is the worst offender and the original proposal omitted it.
- [ ] **Decide the MTP config question**: our GQA-4 / 4-draft-token setup makes item A worth ~0.
      Either measure at a config where it pays (more draft tokens, which also raises acceptance
      length) or report item A as config-dependent with the band table above.

#### B2 RESULT (2026-10-09): epilogue fusion is bounded at ~6%, and the split's own scatters are 1.2%

`drv/b2_top.py` on the B1b trace, sorting by **launch count** rather than time -- B1b's analyzer
sorted by time, which hides the fusion targets behind a few large GEMMs. 1644.3 ms kernel time.

| kernels with median duration | launches | ms | share of kernel time |
|---|---|---|---|
| < 5 us | 23448 | 104.94 | **6.4%** |
| < 10 us | 28887 | 186.16 | 11.3% |
| < 20 us | 30686 | 213.14 | 13.0% |

**So epilogue fusion's ceiling is ~6% of kernel time**, and the realistic figure is well under
that: fusing cannot delete the arithmetic, only the per-launch overhead (~2 us of a 3.4 us
kernel). Top offenders by count are mostly MODEL-FORWARD ops, not spec-specific:
3782 `fused_add_rmsnorm` (med 3.4 us), 2216 `vectorized_gather`, 1891 `fused_rope`,
1891 `act_and_mul` (48.24 ms, the largest single epilogue cost), 1771 `FillFunctor` (med 1.4 us),
1682 `PersistentVariableLengthMergeStates`, 1680 `store_kvcache`.

**The actionable finding is self-inflicted: `index_copy_kernel_impl`, 1680 launches, 19.65 ms =
1.2% of kernel time.** That is the split's own two scatters per layer (28 layers x 60 steps),
plus some of the 1771 `FillFunctor` launches from the `empty_like` pattern -- overhead the split
itself added, sitting inside its own -5% regression.

**Removed in `sglang-up@91955d929`.** In a merged 4-mode batch the token layout is
`[prefill chunk | verify rows]`, so FA3 rows form a contiguous **prefix** and FA2 rows a
contiguous **suffix**; both are then plain views, so each executor reads its `q` slice and writes
its output slice directly and the scatters disappear. Contiguity is **checked, not assumed** --
both row sets must be contiguous ranges whose token spans start at 0, end at `tok_total` and
abut, else the scatter path is kept. CPU-verified on three shapes: a merged 4-mode batch yields
spans `(0,2047)+(2047,2075)`; an interleaved partition is refused; a verify-first ordering still
qualifies with FA3 as the suffix. A `fused_split_views` counter records how often the view path
fires so an A/B can confirm it rather than infer it.

- [x] **B2 bound measured: ~6.4% of kernel time** in sub-5us launches; mostly model-forward
      elementwise, not spec epilogue.
- [x] **Split's own scatters identified (1.2%) and eliminated** via contiguous-span views
      (`91955d929`). Not yet measured in-server.
- [ ] **B2b. Re-run the warmed A/B with the view path** -- the first change in this whole
      sequence that removes measured, attributable overhead rather than a hypothesised one.
- [ ] **B2c. `tma_store_wait` cross-role backfill and multicast** -- still untested, and now
      bounded by the ~6% figure above, so expectations should be set accordingly.

#### B2b RESULT (2026-10-09): **the batch-shape hypothesis is REFUTED.** The two-executor split loses at every shape

`sglang-up@91955d929` (+ view-counter logging), driver `drv/split_perf_mtp.sh` with
`MRR=96 MC=64 RR=24 NP=240`, per-arm warmup, arm order reversed with `base` LAST, graphs off.
Raw: `/dev/shm/w/split_perf_mtp_results.txt`.

| arm (exec order) | tok/s | Mean TTFT | P99 TTFT | Mean ITL | P99 ITL | views | fa2_rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| skipplan | 12169.84 | 245.74 | 2040.75 | 20.81 | 86.17 | 6001 | 62 |
| noguard_m0 | 13225.27 | 164.52 | -- | 19.23 | -- | 6001 | 62 |
| guard_on | 13192.77 | 160.64 | -- | 19.21 | -- | 5501 | 63 |
| **base (split OFF)** | **14545.47** | **152.33** | -- | **17.63** | -- | -- | -- |

Best split arm is **-9.1% tok/s**, **+9.1% mean ITL**, **+8.0% mean TTFT** against base.
Accept length identical (2.07) in all arms, so the arms are comparable.

**RETRACTION: the batch-shape hypothesis is refuted.** I argued that the split regressed because
the server produced `fa2_rows=7` while the isolated 1.224x was measured at `fa2_rows=40`, and
that a decode-rich batch would flip the sign. This run has **`fa2_rows=62`** -- *more* favourable
than the harness shape -- and the split is **worse** (-9.1%) than at `fa2_rows=7` (-8.4%). Shape
is not the explanation. Recorded in place; the hypothesis was reasonable and is wrong.

**Also settled: the scatters were not the explanation either.** `views=6001` confirms the
scatter-free path fired on every dispatch (the counter is logged, so this is measured, not
inferred), removing the 1.2%-of-kernel-time `index_copy_` cost that B2 identified. The
regression did not improve.

**And `skip_base_plan` HURTS.** With `base_plan_skipped` confirmed firing, that arm is the worst
of the four (12169.84 tok/s, P99 TTFT 2040.75 ms). Skipping the full-batch plan leaves
`forward_metadata` pointing at wrappers that were never planned, so any layer where the dispatch
declines falls back onto an unplanned wrapper. The knob should be removed, not tuned.

**What is now established about the two-executor approach, after four independent attempts to
rescue it:** per-step host cost (preallocation -- within noise), the redundant full-batch plan
(skipping it is worse), the scatters (removed, no change), and batch shape (refuted). The
structure itself is the problem.

**The mechanism, and why it motivates K1 specifically.** flashinfer's single
`BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheKernel` is already a persistent varlen kernel that schedules work
items across the WHOLE batch internally. Splitting that batch into two launches throws away that
global load balancing and adds a second kernel tail, and FA3's advantage on the one prefill row
does not cover the loss. The isolated 1.224x was measured against a different baseline (one
persistent wrapper on a synthetic batch), which is why it did not transfer.

**This is the strongest argument yet for the fused single kernel:** only a single-grid design
keeps **one launch and one scheduler** while still specialising the mainloop per row class. The
two-executor variant -- the goal's "also acceptable" fallback -- is now measured as a dead end at
serving scale, and the remaining kernel hope rests entirely on K1.

- [x] **B2b DONE: split is -9.1% at the decode-rich shape with scatters removed.** Batch-shape
      hypothesis retracted; scatters and plan-skipping eliminated as explanations.
- [x] **`SGLANG_FUSED_SKIP_BASE_PLAN` is harmful** -- remove rather than tune.
- [ ] **Remove the two-executor dispatch from the default path** once K1 lands, or keep it only
      behind a flag as the measured-negative baseline it now is.

#### K1 scoped from 0.7's headers (2026-10-09): the reduction was REDESIGNED, not relocated

Read `flashinfer/data/include/flashinfer/attention/scheduler.cuh` on the installed 0.7 wheel.
`HolisticPlanInfo<NUM_TASKS>` now carries, **per task**: `q_indptr`, `kv_indptr`,
**`partial_indptr`**, `q_len`, `kv_len`, `q_start`, `kv_start`, `kv_end`, `kv_head_idx`,
`work_indptr` (10 fields); and **shared**: `len_kv_chunk`, `partial_o`, `partial_lse`,
`merge_indptr`, `merge_o_indices`, `num_qo_len` (6 fields).

**The four group tables the kernel indexes are gone and replaced.** 0.3.1 exposed
`group_id` / `group_nchunks` / `group_row_begin` / `group_nrows` -- group counters the kernel's
just-in-time reduction walked. 0.7 instead exposes a per-task **`partial_indptr`** plus shared
**`merge_indptr` / `merge_o_indices`**, i.e. the conventional split-KV merge-list pattern. So the
JIT reduction must be **rewritten against a different scheme**, not re-pointed at moved fields.
This is the outcome flagged as possible before starting: *"if 0.7 removed those tables because
the reduction itself was redesigned, I'll report that rather than force a port against a model
that no longer exists."* It was redesigned.

**The arithmetic confirms the model exactly.** `ToVector()` length is `2 + NUM_TASKS*10 + 6`:
**NUM_TASKS=2 gives 28**, which is precisely the plan length 0.7's `BatchAttention` produced and
the kernel rejected. So 0.7 also dropped from **3 tasks to 2**. **CORRECTION (2026-10-09):** I earlier wrote that `NUM_SHARED_ARGS = 8` while only 6 shared
fields are pushed, calling it the same count-vs-reality inconsistency 0.3.1 had at 16-vs-14.
**That was wrong.** Enumerating `ToVector()` mechanically gives **8** shared pushes --
`num_blks_x`, `num_blks_y`, `len_kv_chunk`, `partial_o`, `partial_lse`, `merge_indptr`,
`merge_o_indices`, `num_qo_len` -- and 10 per task. I had counted only the 6 trailing fields and
missed `num_blks_x`/`num_blks_y`, which are shared too. So in 0.7 the arithmetic is **consistent**:
`NUM_SHARED_ARGS + NUM_TASKS*NUM_TASK_ARGS = 8 + 2*10 = 28`, exactly the observed plan length.
The lesson I drew from it ("never trust the constants") does not apply to 0.7, and the length
guard our patch adds using that formula is therefore correct here.

**Revised K1 content, in order:**

- [x] **K1a RESOLVED by measurement (2026-10-09): DROP the JIT reduction, use 0.7's scheduled
      merge.** Read the kernel's actual reduction call
      (`include/flashinfer/attention/persistent_fa3_fused.cuh:686-689`): it passes
      `partial_o`, `partial_lse`, `merge_indptr`, `merge_o_indices` -- **all of which 0.7 still
      has** -- *plus* `group_row_begin`, `group_nrows`, `group_kv_head`, `group_nchunks`,
      `group_counter`, which 0.7 dropped. Those five exist **only** for the in-kernel
      just-in-time rendezvous: an atomic `group_counter` against `group_nchunks` so the last
      chunk to finish performs the merge itself and no separate merge kernel is launched.
      0.7 instead schedules the merge as its own kernel -- and that kernel is visible in the B1b
      trace: **`PersistentVariableLengthMergeStatesKernel`, 1682 launches, 10.66 ms = 0.6% of
      kernel time.** So the entire cost that JIT reduction removes is **bounded at 0.6% of GPU
      time**, which is far below the +/-1.5-3% noise floor.
      **Therefore K1a is not a port of the group tables at all.** Port the fused kernel to write
      partials and let 0.7's scheduled merge reduce them, exactly as 0.7's own `BatchAttention`
      does. This removes the need to reconstruct any group table, removes the atomic rendezvous,
      and removes the recorded split-KV defect where `group_counter` can never reach
      `group_nchunks - 1` when causal masking leaves a chunk with no work item.
      **On the paper's technique:** just-in-time reduction is one of the two ideas in *Taming
      Dynamism on GPUs*. Measuring its ceiling at 0.6% here is the honest way to "think carefully
      about how it fits our story" rather than copying it -- on this workload it does not pay, and
      saying so is more useful than reimplementing it. If a later measurement shows the merge
      kernel growing (more split-KV chunks at longer context), it can be revisited with a known
      target to beat.

#### INCIDENT (2026-10-09): both fixes that made the fused kernel PASS were pod-only and were LOST

Starting K1-0 surfaced this. The two fixes recorded in this doc as making the fused kernel PASS
the causal fp32 reference at every `sm_split` -- `MaskMode::kNone` -> `kCausal` in `PKT`, and the
`cluster_tile_q` guard under `FUSED_GRID` -- **were applied directly to the pod's copy of
flashinfer and never committed**. The local checkout `/opt/tiger/flashinfer` at `b0563ae` still
had `MaskMode::kNone` (0 occurrences of `kCausal`) and the unguarded
`cluster_tile_q = gridDim.x * CTA_TILE_Q`, byte-identical to 0.7's line 242.

That pod's trial went to `done` and its tmpfs is gone, so **those fixes existed nowhere in
version control.** They are recoverable only because this doc recorded them verbatim, including
the exact replacement expression. Restored and committed as `flashinfer@c496afd` before the port
begins, so the 0.7 rebase starts from a correct kernel instead of silently re-deriving both bugs.

Consequences worth stating:

  longer existed anywhere.** It was already unusable as evidence (flashinfer 0.3.1, 20-arg
  extension); this makes it unreproducible for a second, independent reason.

  part of K1-0: every code change this doc claims must be verified present in git before being
  relied on.
* **Process fix:** edits made on the pod have to be committed locally the same session. The
  push-patch-apply loop used for sglang does this correctly; the flashinfer tree was being edited
  in place on the pod and so bypassed it.

#### K1b DONE / K1c MEASURED (2026-10-09)

**K1b: `persistent.cuh` ported** -- `flashinfer@ed1be8a`, as an include **overlay**
(`port07/include/flashinfer/attention/`) in front of the wheel's bundled headers, so 0.7 supplies
every file except the ones we override. Mixing the 0.3.1 checkout and the 0.7 wheel on one
include path is what silently reintroduces the plan-layout mismatch, hence the overlay.
Our 16-hunk diff applies **11**; the **5 rejects are all JIT-reduction machinery**
(`MergeGroupJIT`, the `s_merge_flag` handshake, the `group_id != nullptr` rendezvous, the
`__threadfence` dance) and are **dropped by design** per K1a. Verified: `FUSED_GRID` role
indexing present, the recovered `cluster_tile_q` guard at line 290, and **zero** residual
`MergeGroupJIT`/`s_merge_flag`/`group_counter` references.

**K1c: `scheduler.cuh` measured -- 15 of 22 hunks apply, 7 reject.** Verified invariants after
the fuzzy apply (fuzz 2-3 on a redesigned file can land a hunk in the wrong place, so this was
checked rather than assumed): **no group tables re-added** (0 occurrences), `HolisticPlanInfo<2>`
still used by 0.7's `BatchAttention`, and the length guard our patch adds is correct for 0.7 (see
the correction above).

**The 7 rejects are the real K1c work, and they are NOT droppable.** They sit in
`HolisticPlanInfo` (3 hunks) and `TwoStageHolisticPlan` (4 hunks), and they are what adds the
**4-task plan and the unified-wgmma fields**. That matters because the 4th task *is* the fused
design: it is the class whose work items FA3's mainloop pulls through
`UnifiedWgmmaTileScheduler`, i.e. FA3's work expressed as a task inside the same plan as FA2's.
0.7's `BatchAttention` only ever builds a 2-task plan, so the fused kernel needs **our own
4-task plan builder** on top of 0.7's struct definitions -- which is precisely what our +439
lines were on 0.3.1.

So K1c decomposes as:

- [x] **K1c1 DONE, and the design changed: a PRIVATE plan struct, not an extension of
      0.7's.** `flashinfer@79a79a7` adds `port07/include/flashinfer/attention/fused_plan.cuh`
      defining `FusedPlanInfo<NUM_TASKS>` -- 0.7's fields plus `batch_idx_offset` per task and
      six shared fields (cluster cursor and counts for cross-role backfill, `max_splits_fa3`, the
      compact FA3 request list, `num_fa3_clusters` kept last because the harness reads the chosen
      split as `plan_info[-1]`). **11 per task / 14 shared, verified self-consistent by
      enumeration** (pushes == reads == constants), **58 entries at `NUM_TASKS=4`**.
      **`scheduler.cuh` is no longer overlaid at all.**
      *Why the design changed:* extending `HolisticPlanInfo` in place makes it 36 entries at
      `NUM_TASKS=2` against stock 0.7's 28, and `BatchAttention._plan_info` is produced by
      **flashinfer's own JIT-compiled module**, not ours -- so the two sides would disagree and
      the kernel would reject every plan, the same failure class as the original
      `28 entries, expected 56 or 68`. On the 0.3.1 *source tree* this could not happen, because
      flashinfer's JIT compiled `BatchAttention` from the same modified headers. With the 0.7
      *wheel* that coupling is gone. Chosen over the alternative (inject the overlay into
      flashinfer's JIT so `BatchAttention` sees the extended struct), which is less code but
      leaves us coupled to their internal build on every upgrade -- and releases have already
      broken this work twice (plan-struct redesign, `vector_sparse` helper removal).
      *Consequence:* 0.7's `HolisticPlanInfo`, `TwoStageHolisticPlan` and `BatchAttention` are
      untouched, so **K1c3 is satisfied by construction** -- there is no overlay to perturb them.

#### K1b2 progress: nvcc errors 7 -> 2, both remaining ones diagnosed (2026-10-09)

`port07/tests/nvcc_check.sh` (merged 0.7 + overlay include tree, sm_90a, C++20) on each step:

| step | commit | errors |
|---|---|---|
| fuzzy-applied baseline | -- | **7** |
| barrier ids carved into `fused_barriers.cuh` | `flashinfer@34e5cf0` | **5** |

Both remaining errors are now understood exactly, and neither needs a design decision:

1. **`thr_local_kv_offset` undefined (overlay line 433).** 0.7 **split this into two arrays** --
   `thr_local_kv_offset_k` and `thr_local_kv_offset_v` (0.7 `persistent.cuh:269,271`) -- and
   passes them separately to `prefetch_offest` / `page_produce_kv` at its lines 328/331. Our code
   (from the FA2 K/V smem-ring work, `f54745e` / `3e41c2d`) still uses one shared array. **Fix:**
   at each use site pass the `_k` variant on the K path and `_v` on the V path. Mechanical, but
   it must follow the buffer rather than be search-replaced, since the `issue` lambda handles both.
2. **`a template declaration is not allowed here` (overlay line 880).** The `KVStagedTraits`
   template, also from the KV-ring commits, was placed by the fuzzy apply **inside a function
   body**, where C++ forbids template declarations. **Fix:** move `KVStagedTraits` and its
   `FLASHINFER_FA2_KV_STAGES_*` / `FLASHINFER_FA2_NUM_MMA_KV_*` macros to namespace scope. This
   is the second structural corruption fuzzy patching introduced (the first put `push_back`
   statements inside an error-message expression in `scheduler.cuh`).

- [x] **K1b2 DONE (2026-10-09): `persistent.cuh` COMPILES against 0.7.** `NVCC_PARSE_OK` from
      `port07/tests/nvcc_check.sh` (merged 0.7 + overlay include tree, sm_90a, `-std=c++20`,
      `--expt-relaxed-constexpr`). Error progression, one commit per fix:
      **7 -> 5 -> 2 -> 0**.

      | fix | commit | errors after |
      |---|---|---|
      | barrier ids carved into `fused_barriers.cuh` (avoids overlaying 0.7's 4871-line `prefill.cuh`) | `flashinfer@34e5cf0` | 5 |
      | `kNoClusterOverride` + `cluster_override` / `tid_base` parameters hand-applied to `Run` | `flashinfer@933a655` | 2 |
      | K/V offset arrays separated, each prefetched with its own strides | `flashinfer@0d34c00` | 1 |
      | `KVStagedTraits` + macros moved to namespace scope | `flashinfer@2c79439` | **0** |

      **A latent bug in OUR code, surfaced by the port.** 0.7 split `thr_local_kv_offset` into
      `_k` and `_v`. Porting our KV-ring lambda onto that showed it called `prefetch_offest`
      **once with K's strides** (`k_stride_page/h/n`) and reused the result for the **V**
      `page_produce_kv`. That is only correct while V's strides equal K's -- and is plausibly why
      0.7 split the arrays. Fixed by issuing two prefetches. This changes what addresses the V
      loads read whenever the strides differ, so it is a correctness fix, not a rename.

      **Second structural corruption from fuzzy patching.** The `FLASHINFER_FA2_KV_STAGES_*`
      macros and `KVStagedTraits` had been placed **inside** the following struct template, where
      C++ forbids template declarations. nvcc said only *"a template declaration is not allowed
      here"*, naming neither the template nor the enclosing scope. With the `push_back`
      statements it put inside an error-message expression in `scheduler.cuh`, that is two
      corruptions, **both invisible to symbol greps and findable only by compiling**. The
      remaining files are hand-ported.

         unified reduction's per-item fields cannot ride along it. Note this probes the
         SCHEDULER's own `group_id` field, which we keep in

         dropped, and conflating the two would wrongly suggest this trait can go.

         packed-GQA loader is one warp issuing its own `cp.async` completed with
         `cp.async.mbarrier.arrive`, which tracks only the issuing thread's copies, so all 32
         lanes must arrive for themselves. Arming for 32 is what lets Q complete WITHOUT a
         `cp.async` group drain -- `commit_group` otherwise sweeps the producer's in-flight KV
         copies into Q's group, and committed groups retire in order, so a drain waits on the

- [x] **K1d3 (2026-10-09, `flashinfer@4ef2407`). FA2+FA3 co-inclusion in one TU is legal

      because its upstream carried `...Sm90` suffixes on the Hopper spellings; 0.7 dropped them
      because nothing needed them. Five collisions, in `namespace flashinfer`:

      | name | nature | resolution |
      |---|---|---|
      | `AttentionVariantBase` | different types in both trees | Hopper -> `...Sm90`, alias behind the flag |
      | `SharedStorageQKVO` | different types in both trees | Hopper -> `...Sm90`; our `persistent.cuh` wants the **FA2** one (its parameter list matches `prefill.cuh`, not `kernel_traits.cuh`) |
      | `DefaultAttention` / `DefaultFP8Attention` | different types | Hopper -> `...Sm90`, alias behind the flag |
      | `StandardAttention` / `LogitsSoftCap` / `StandardFP8Attention` | 0.7 declares `StandardAttention` in **`mla.cuh`** too, where the fused TU resolved it | Hopper -> `...Sm90`; nvcc calls this *ambiguous*, not redefined |
      | the four `DEFINE_HAS_MEMBER` probes | **identical** in both trees | `FLASHINFER_SHARED_HAS_MEMBER_PROBES`, which is 0.3.1 upstream's own mechanism |
      | `REGISTER_LOGITS_TRANSFORM` / `LOGITS_MASK` / `QUERY_TRANSFORM` / `KEY_TRANSFORM` | bodies differ **only in the name of a template type parameter** (`Params` vs `MainloopParams`), so whichever wins compiles both trees identically -- a warning, not a correctness hazard | guarded **per-macro on both sides**, not per-file: FA2 defines two macros Hopper lacks (`REGISTER_M_D_UPDATE`, `REGISTER_OUTPUT_TRANSFORM`) and a whole-file guard would strand them |

      A tree-wide rename is **not** available: every stock FA3 module is generated with
      `variant_name = "DefaultAttention<...>"`, so it would break all of them. Hence the
      aliases, dropped only by `-DFLASHINFER_SM90_SUPPRESS_UNSUFFIXED_NAMES=1`, which must be a
      TU-wide **compile flag** rather than a `#define` in `persistent_fa3_fused.cuh` --
      whichever header reaches `hopper/variant_helper.cuh` first wins, and in our own test TU
      that is `fused_plan.cuh`. Without the flag the build fails loudly on the aliases; it can
      never silently bind to the FA2 type of the same name. Renaming a struct also renames its
      **constructors**: leaving them behind turns each into a deduction guide.

- [x] **K1j ANSWERED (2026-10-09). No, and it structurally cannot in 0.7's own form.**
      Verified by reading the launch site rather than grepping for a call: `persistent.cuh:929`
      launches **one cooperative kernel**

      ```
      PersistentKernelTemplate<BlockBatchPagedAttentionPersistent<KTraits1, Params>,
                               BlockBatchPagedAttentionPersistent<KTraits2, Params>,
                               BlockBatchReductionPersistent<ReductionKTraits>>
      ...
      cudaLaunchCooperativeKernel((void*)kernel, nblks, nthrs, args, smem_size, stream)
      ```

      so in 0.7 the merge is a **third role inside the same grid**, and the **cooperative**
      launch is what gives it the grid-wide sync to run only after every partial is written. Our
      fused dispatcher launches `cudaLaunchKernel` / `cudaLaunchKernelExC` with the three FA2
      runners plus FA3 and **no reduction role**, non-cooperatively. So there is nothing to
      "add a call to" -- the two designs differ in grid structure.

      **Decision: launch the reduction as a SEPARATE kernel after the attention grid**, not as a
      fourth role. Reasons, in order:
      - A cooperative launch constrains the grid to what fits co-resident, which is exactly the
        quantity `sm_split` pre-assignment is manipulating. Making the fused kernel cooperative
        would couple the SM split to an occupancy constraint and is the opposite of the design.
      - K1a already priced this: flashinfer's scheduled merge is a separate pass at 1682
        launches / 10.66 ms in the B1b trace, and the in-kernel JIT rendezvous that avoided it
        was measured at a 0.6%-of-GPU-time ceiling -- below the +/-1.5-3% serving noise floor.
        So a separate pass is the already-measured choice, not a concession.
      - `BlockBatchReductionPersistent::Run` is a `__device__` member, so a standalone launch
        needs only a thin `__global__` wrapper plus `num_merge_rows` as `num_packed_qo_len`.

- [x] **K1k DONE (2026-10-09, `flashinfer@641ef1b`). The reduction is launched as a separate
      pass after the fused attention grid.** Device kernels on the unified TU **10 -> 15**, so
      the wrapper is genuinely instantiated rather than discarded by an `if constexpr` -- the
      failure mode that made three earlier green compiles mean less than they looked.

      **The grid shape was the trap, and it fails silently.** `Run()` derives

      ```
      worker_id   = blockIdx.y * num_warps + warp_idx
      num_workers = gridDim.x * gridDim.y * gridDim.z * num_warps
      ```

      so the stride counts every block while the id varies only in **Y**. Launched as the obvious
      `(N, 1, 1)`, every block computes the **same** `worker_id` and every row not congruent to
      it is never written -- the identical silent partial-coverage signature to fixture 2's
      511/512, with no error and no assert. Blocks therefore go in `gridDim.Y`, `x = z = 1`.

      The launcher no-ops when `num_merge_rows == 0` (the common decode-only case). Passing the
      batch's row count instead of the plan's compacted split-row count would make the merge
      visit unsplit rows, whose `num_index_sets` of 0 fills their output with **zeros** over the
      direct write -- the rows needing no merge would be exactly the ones it destroyed.

      | fixture | kv | merge rows | result |

      | `fa3` | 2048 | 1032 | wrong numbers (44.84), **no fault** |

      **SANITIZED (2026-10-09): a NEGATIVE partial index -- a partial write on an unsplit row.**
      `MODE=fa3_1chunk`, `CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1`, a new signature (4 bytes, not 16):

      ```
      Invalid __global__ write of size 4 bytes
      by thread (128,0,0) in block (8,0,0)
      Access to 0x7f603fffffd4 is out of bounds
      and is 44 bytes BEFORE the nearest allocation ... of size 1,073,741,824 bytes
      at void flashinfer::FusedFA3PersistentKernel
      ```

      Three facts pin it: the 1 GB allocation is the driver's **float** workspace, so the target
      is the partial buffers; a **4-byte** write is `partial_lse` (float), not `partial_o` (bf16,
      written 16 B at a time); and it lands **before** the base, so the index is **negative**.
      `-44/4 = -11`, which at `num_kv_heads=7` is `(-2)*7 + 3` -- a partial row index of −2 at kv
      head 3. **−1 is exactly what `BuildFusedMergeLayout` writes into `partial_indptr` for a row
      it marked UNSPLIT.** So a row the plan says needs no partial is reaching a partial write,
      and the offset arithmetic runs off the front of the buffer.

      Block 8 is below `sm_split=16`, so an FA3-role block -- consistent, since the FA3 epilogue
      gates `store_partial` on `work_tile_info.group_id >= 0`, and `group_id` is now **derived**
      in the scheduler as `(num_kv_chunks > 1) ? 0 : -1` from
      `ceil_div(kv_len, len_kv_chunk[0])`. For this fixture that is `ceil_div(128,128) = 1`, so
      the gate should be **closed**. One of those two inputs is therefore not what the plan
      wrote -- the same class as the five plan index-space bugs, and settled by printing what the
      FA3 scheduler actually read, from every block.

      **CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED (`flashinfer@c7fdd92`): the `WorkTileInfo` aggregate initialiser
      was misaligned.** The struct is `(..., partial_indptr, group_id, kv_chunk_idx,
      num_kv_chunks, ...)` but the positional initialiser listed `kv_chunk_idx` **before**
      `group_id`, so `group_id` silently received the **chunk index** -- 0 for the first chunk,
      which opens the `group_id >= 0` gate on **every** row. The FA3 epilogue then called
      `store_partial` for rows the plan had marked unsplit with `partial_indptr = -1`.

      The trace showed the contradiction directly instead of by inference: all 16 FA3 blocks
      reported `group_id=0 chunks=1 partial_indptr=-1`, three values that cannot hold together
      since `group_id` is derived as `(nchunks > 1) ? 0 : -1` from the same quantity printed as
      `chunks=1`. It also matches the sanitizer arithmetic exactly -- 4 bytes 44 B before the base
      is `(-2)*7 + 3` at `num_kv_heads=7`.

      Now **designated initialisers**, like the three other aggregates this port has had to fix
      for the same reason (sparse mainloop `Arguments`, epilogue `Arguments`,
      `UnifiedWgmmaPlanPtrs`). **Four positional aggregates misaligned in one port.**

      | fixture | before | after |
      |---|---|---|
      | `fa2` | PASS | **PASS** rel 0.002126, 0/258 |
      | `fa3_1chunk` | **illegal access** | no fault, rel 3.076e+06, 256/256 |
      | `fa3` | 44.84 | 45.1 |
      | `mixed` | 41.67 | 45.44, 256/258 (FA2 rows pass) |

      `BlockBatchReductionPersistent::Run` resolves its destination as
      `o_indices[packed_qo_idx] + kv_head_idx * gqa_group_size`, indexing `v_merged` viewed as
      `[qo_len, num_kv_heads, gqa_group_size, head_dim]`. So the value must be a FLAT row index
      over (token, qo_head) with head-in-group folded in:
      `(token_base + token) * (num_kv_heads * G) + head_in_group`. We pushed the **token index
      alone** -- unscaled by `num_qo_heads`, and dropping `head_in_group` entirely, so four
      consecutive packed rows of one token collapsed onto one destination.

      **It explains the old symptom exactly, which is why I trust the diagnosis:** values 0..31
      plus `kv_head * G <= 24` land in flat rows 0..55 of an 896-row space -- token 0 and token 1
      only. The fixture reported precisely `2/32 rows non-zero`.

      - `store_partial`'s O slot `(partial_indptr + r*chunks + kv_chunk_idx) * num_kv_heads +

        construction. Addressing on the partial side is verified by reading, not assumed.
      - Row counts are consistent: `fa3` reports `num_merge_rows=1032` = 8 tiles x 128 packed rows

      - **`FLASHINFER_FUSED_NO_MERGE=1` gives 0/32 and 0/256 rows non-zero.** So there is NO double

        from the reduction. The direct-write path is exonerated for split rows, and the residual is
        entirely the reduction's inputs or its arithmetic.
      - The reduction launch is a thin wrapper over 0.7's `BlockBatchReductionPersistent::Run`,
        which self-covers via a grid-stride loop over `num_packed_qo_len * num_kv_heads`, so grid
        sizing cannot be the cause of the missing rows (it could only make it slow).

        state is in **log2** space, and FA3's `OnlineSoftmax` with `WITH_SCALE` also produces
        log2-scale LSE. The two agree, so this is not a base-e/base-2 mismatch. Both `store()` and
        `store_partial()` write `lse(mi)` with no conversion, so they cannot differ from each
        other either.

      So `store_partial` must write a *finalized* `tOrO`. If `attention_updater.finalize(tOrO)` is
      not called before `store_partial` on the split path -- or is called twice -- every merged row
      is off by a row-sum factor, which is exactly the residual's shape: all rows present, values
      off by O(1), and the one row of 32 that passes being where a single chunk dominates so the
      factor is ~1. Check the call sequence in `prefill_sm90.cuh` around the `store_partial` site
      against the `store()` site.

      **Normalization-ordering suspect: REFUTED immediately (2026-10-10).** The dispatch in

      `store_partial` and to `store`, selected by `wrote_partial` -- one store per work item,
      never both. So the normalization state cannot differ between the split and direct paths, and
      `finalize` ordering is not the cause. (Also confirmed: the double-store that once
      double-arrived on `EpilogueBarrier` is gated out, consistent with the `NO_MERGE` result
      showing no direct write for split rows.)

      equals `chunks >= 2` for every merged row (our CSR pushes `chunks` per row cumulatively
      across groups, so the group boundaries are not special), and the merge's bypass for
      `num_index_sets <= 1` therefore cannot be swallowing merged rows. `merge_o_indices` (1024
      entries) and `merge_indptr` (1025) are indexed by the same ordinal.

      | single warp (before) | 0.2470 | 1 |
      | all MMA threads | **0.2183 (-12%)** | **8** |

      win is not worth an 80%-failure kernel. Reverted, and the revert re-verified at 1/10.

      refilling it for the next work item while the consumer reads it -- widening the set of
      readers widens that window. The `store_partial_zero` vectorisation (uint4 instead of
      element-at-a-time) was kept; it is not implicated.

      only the delta is readable). Then optimise whichever dominates, respecting the sO lifetime

      **Parameter-order bug found and fixed in the process.** `AttentionKernelTraits` is
      `<USE_TMA_LOAD_KV, HEAD_DIM_QK, HEAD_DIM_VO, CTA_Q, CTA_KV, NUM_STAGES, ...>`, and the
      original call site was `<false, 128, 128, 128, 128, STAGES, ...>` -- **all four identical, so
      the ordering was unverifiable from the call site.** My first attempt set position 3 and so
      changed `HEAD_DIM_VO` to 64, tripping `static_assert(HEAD_DIM_QK == HEAD_DIM_VO)`. Same
      hazard as the positional aggregate initialisers fixed earlier in this port: identical values
      hide an ordering until one of them changes. Order now read off `kernel_traits.cuh` and
      recorded at the call site.

      **The new non-finite guard earned its keep immediately** -- all three failing arms here
      produce NaN, which the harness would have reported as `bad rows 0 ... PASS` this morning.

      **[x] RESOLVED, and it found a HARNESS HOLE worse than the probe (2026-10-10). The
      packed-Q gather is NOT the bottleneck: it costs ~1.5%.**

      The one-line check -- do the two arms' outputs differ at all -- answered it immediately. An
      output fingerprint (`absmax`, `sum`, `nonzero`) showed:

      | arm | fingerprint | reported verdict |
      |---|---|---|
      | `SKIP_PACKED_Q=0` | absmax 0.01721, sum 97.56 | PASS 0.003279 |
      | `SKIP_PACKED_Q=1` | **absmax nan, sum nan** | **"PASS 0.002069, 0/258"** |

      **The harness was silently passing NaN.** NaN comparisons are all False, so a NaN output
      scored `rel = nan`, failed the `rel > tol` test, and came back as `bad rows 0`. Every verdict
      this harness has ever printed was therefore unsound for any arm that produced non-finite
      output -- a much worse defect than the probe I was chasing. Fixed with an explicit
      non-finite guard that fails before any per-row norm is computed; null-cased both ways
      (`SKIP=1` now reports `NON-FINITE OUTPUT: 730112 of 924672 elements`, `SKIP=0` still PASSes,
      and the normal arm passed 6/6 afterwards).

      **With the skip confirmed effective, the gather's cost is bounded at ~1.5%**: 0.2927 ms
      (normal) vs 0.2884 ms (gather removed) at `SM_SPLIT=128`. Caveat worth stating: the skip arm
      computes on NaNs, and NaN arithmetic need not take the same time as normal arithmetic -- but
      the loads themselves are structurally gone, so the gather is exonerated as the cause of the
      4x gap. **This was the prime suspect** (it replaced TMA with a per-row `cp.async` and its own
      comments call it slow), so the 4x lives elsewhere.

      **Where the 4x must therefore be, in order of remaining suspicion:**
      1. `FA3_STAGES=1` -- a single-stage K/V pipeline against a baseline that uses 2. No
         prefetch overlap at all, which is the kind of factor that costs multiples rather than
         percents. `STAGES=2` cannot launch at these traits (a smem limit), so this needs the
         traits revisited -- smaller `CTA_Q` or `CTA_KV` to buy the second stage.
      2. The scalar per-row O stores in `store_partial` and `write_packed`.
      3. The baseline is flashinfer's own tuned FA3 at full occupancy; ours is a persistent
         kernel holding 128 of 132 SMs with one-stage traits.

      **[~] Race hunt (2026-10-10): ONE source found and fixed; a residual race remains at
      1-in-20. The fix is confirmed by the results becoming DETERMINISTIC when they pass.**

      **Localised first:** the failing row is **row 0 of the FA3 request** (the two FA2 rows, 256
      and 257, are always clean). Under bottom-right causal with kv=2048 / qo=256, token 0 sees
      the **fewest** keys -- 1793 of 2048 -- so it is the row most likely to own a chunk lying
      entirely beyond the diagonal.

      **Bug found: a fully masked split chunk never wrote its partial slot.** Such an item hits
      `num_kv_tiles <= 0` and took `store_zero` + `continue`. But the merge counts the chunk
      regardless -- `EnumerateFusedWorkItems` chunks uniformly with no causal adjustment, by
      design, so the count matches what sized the slab and built `merge_indptr`. So the reduction
      read `partial_lse` at an untouched slot (0.0 in a freshly zeroed workspace) and folded a
      zero O in with weight `2^(0 - lse_true)`. At a true LSE near 6.6 that is a ~1% dilution --
      and the measured failure was rel **0.03311** on row 0. `store_zero` was doubly wrong here:
      it writes the FINAL O, not the partial slab, through a token-indexed mapping that is also
      wrong on the packed path.

      Fixed with `store_partial_zero`, which writes the item's slot with **-inf LSE** (the merge's
      identity: `2^(-inf - m) == 0`) and zero O.

      **Evidence the fix is real, and it is not the pass/fail count:** before it, passing runs
      returned rel err scattered over 0.003273 / 0.004544 / 0.004985 / 0.003337 / 0.005239 across
      splits. After it, **every passing run returns an identical 0.003279 at every split**. The
      output is now deterministic when correct, which is exactly what removing an
      uninitialised-read would do -- and a far better signal than a pass count.

      **Double-execution hypothesis REFUTED (2026-10-10).** Counted the scheduler's per-work-item
      dispatch in the co-resident configuration (`mixed`, `SM_SPLIT=48`): **896 `[sched]` lines,
      896 distinct `work_idx`, 0 duplicated**, in each of 6 runs. 896 is exactly right -- 8 q
      tiles x 7 kv heads x 16 chunks -- so every item is dispatched exactly once and cross-role
      backfill is not handing work to two blocks.
      **Stated caveat:** `FA3_PROBE=1` adds per-item printfs that serialise execution, so the 6
      passes under it do NOT disprove the race; only the duplication hypothesis is refuted.
      Remaining candidate, untested: ordering between the FA2 roles' writes and the FA3 partial
      slab they share (the epilogue takes `partial_o`/`partial_lse` straight off Runner1's
      persistent params), i.e. a cross-ROLE rather than cross-block hazard.

      **The fix: an absolute causal bound, threaded as a quantity SEPARATE from `kv_len`.** It had
      to be separate because `kv_len` is simultaneously the iteration bound (`get_num_kv_tiles`,
      and `kv_idx >= kv_len`), so widening it would make each chunk read on into later chunks'
      keys. Five files:
      - `unified_wgmma_scheduler.cuh`: `WorkTileInfo::causal_kv_len = kv_len[work_idx] - kv_begin`
        (the request's total kv minus this chunk's base), set in `load()` and both terminal
        returns.
      - `hopper/utils.cuh`: `fused_causal_kv_len(work_tile_info, kv_len)` with a
        `fused_has_causal_kv_len` detector -- **detected, not required**, because upstream's
        scheduler has no such field and `prefill_sm90.cuh` serves both. Returns `kv_len` when
        absent, so every non-split and upstream path is bit-identical to before.
      - `sparse_mainloop.cuh`: `get_num_kv_tiles(..., causal_kv_len = -1)`, and `load()` passes
        the same value -- **load and mma must agree on the tile count or the pipeline deadlocks.**
      - `mainloop_mma.cuh`: `col_limit_right` / `col_limit_left` use it.
      - `prefill_sm90.cuh`: four call sites (two `get_num_kv_tiles`, two `mma_f16`).

      `min(kv_len, col_limit_right)` then does the right thing for all three cases without extra
      logic: chunks before the diagonal get a bound >= the chunk length so nothing is masked, the
      diagonal chunk masks correctly, and chunks beyond the diagonal get a bound <= 0.

      **[x] SPLIT-KV ROOT CAUSE FOUND (2026-10-10): the causal mask is applied CHUNK-RELATIVE,
      so every split chunk masks off keys it should see. Quantitative match to 4 decimals.**

      Found by dumping `partial_o` / `partial_lse` for known merge rows and comparing against a
      Python per-chunk reference -- `partial_o` holds a NORMALIZED per-chunk output, so the
      comparison needs no LSE convention. That is the split no amount of reading could make:

      | row | token | chunk | head | `O_rel` | `lse_got` | ref (log2, 128 keys) |
      |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
      | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0.6347 | **6.60012** | 7.00090 |
      | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0 | 0.6819 | 6.60120 | 7.00105 |
      | 4 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0.6160 | **6.61413** | 6.99852 |
      | 0 | 0 | 0 | 1 | 0.5138 | 6.60130 | 7.00064 |

      **The LSE identifies the key count exactly.** `log2(97) = 6.5999` against `lse_got =
      6.60012` for token 0, and `log2(98) = 6.6147` against `6.61413` for token 1. So each chunk
      sums over `token + 97` keys, not 128.

      **Where 97 comes from:** `col_limit_right(qo_idx) = (qo_idx/G) + 1 + kv_len - qo_len/G`
      with the CHUNK's `kv_len = 128` and `qo_len/G = 32` gives `token + 1 + 128 - 32 = token +
      97`. The bound is being computed **chunk-relative**. The scheduler hands each split item a
      base shifted to its chunk and `kv_len = kv_chunk`, with the comment *"Legal because this
      path is non-causal"* -- but `CAUSAL` is a **compile-time template parameter applied to every
      item**, so once `FA3_CAUSAL=1` was needed for the unsplit path (and it was: that is what
      made `fa3_1chunk` pass), every split chunk started masking against a bound that means
      nothing in chunk-relative coordinates.

      This also explains why split-KV looked broken in so many different ways across the session:
      the error is per-chunk and position-dependent, so it changes with chunk count, q tile and
      request length.

      **Confirms the merge is INNOCENT of the value error.** `merge_o_indices[:6] = [0,1,2,3,28,29]`
      is exactly right under the fixed units (token 0 heads-in-group 0..3, then token 1 -> 1*28+0),
      `merge_indptr` strides by `chunks = 16`, and the slot arithmetic resolves correctly. The
      merge was faithfully combining partials that were already wrong.

      **[ ] The fix, and it is a design item rather than one line.** The causal bound must be
      absolute, not chunk-relative. For a chunk `[kv0, kv1)` of a request with total `kv_total`
      and `qo_tokens`, row `token` may attend keys up to `kv_total - qo_tokens + token`, i.e.
      `kv_total - qo_tokens + token - kv0` within the chunk. Options, in the order I would try:
      1. Pass the chunk base and the request's total kv to the mainloop and compute the bound
         absolutely. Most faithful; needs two more fields through `BlockCoord`.
      2. Have the planner skip chunks entirely beyond the diagonal and mark the rest unmasked,
         masking only the chunk containing the diagonal. Cheaper at runtime, more planner logic,
         and it must agree with the `splits` count the partial slab was sized from.
      Note the interaction with [[packed-gqa-breaks-token-bounds]]: whatever carries the bound
      must stay in TOKEN units while `qo_idx` is a packed row.

      **[ ] Part 2, the remaining defect: the merged values.** All rows are now written and
      `fa2` is unaffected, so this is the reduction's arithmetic or the partials it reads, not
      addressing. Where to look next, in order:
      - `store_partial`'s slab offset `base + r * num_kv_chunks + kv_chunk_idx` against the
        merge's `(indptr[packed_qo_idx] + off) * num_kv_heads + kv_head_idx`. These must agree on
        BOTH the ordering of merge rows and the per-group base; `merge_indptr` is built in
        (group, r) order and `store_partial` uses the group's single base plus `r * chunks`, which
        agrees only if the merge-row ordinal equals `group_order * rows + r`.
      - **`partial_lse`**: a wrong or unwritten LSE gives correctly-addressed rows combined with
        wrong weights -- which is exactly the shape of the residual (all rows present, values
        off by O(1)). `fa3_split` has 16 chunks (kv 2048, chunk 128), so a mis-weighted combine
        across 16 partials would look like this.
      - Why `fa3_multitile` writes only 128 of 256 token rows while `fa3_split` writes all 32 --
        a multi-tile-specific gap in the merge-row ordinal, on top of the value bug.

      **Bug 3 (two sites, one family): the packed-GQA rows break every TOKEN-INDEXED causal
      bound.** Our unified FA3 role tiles over PACKED rows -- (token, head-in-group) pairs --
      because FA3's mainloop validates the tile index against `qo_len`. 0.7's causal arithmetic is
      token-indexed, so both the row index and `qo_len` are G times too large on the q axis. Two
      places had to be corrected, and the token index needs an integer division, so no choice of
      `qo_len` makes the stock expressions right:
      - `mainloop_mma.cuh` `col_limit_right` / `col_limit_left` -- the per-row mask bound. (This
        file is now in the overlay; it was stock 0.7 before, md5 `c82eff57` verified against the
        pod's copy before patching.)
      - `sparse_mainloop.cuh` `get_num_kv_tiles` -- the causal kv-tile count, and this one is why
        most of the output was simply **missing**: at G=4 with 128 tokens (512 packed rows, 4 q
        tiles) the stock bound gives `(0+1)*128 + 128 - 512 = -256` for q tile 0, so
        `num_kv_tiles <= 0` and the body **exits early without storing**. Only q tile 3 survived
        (`512+128-512 = 128`), so exactly 32 of 128 token rows were written and 96 stayed zero.

      Both reduce to 0.7's expression exactly at G=1, which is why the G=1 arms passed either way.

      **How it was localised, and what it cost to not do this first.** The driver's own
      diagnostics said `ours: 32/128 rows non-zero` and `passing rows 96..127` -- one q tile's
      worth, at the LAST tile. A scheduler probe then showed all **28 items dispatched correctly**
      (7 per q tile, `span=1`, `nchunks=1`, `partial=-1` direct-write), which put the defect
      inside the body rather than in the plan or the scheduler. Reading the `[wpk]` store probe
      first -- 14 lines, every one `tile=3` -- would have pointed at the same place immediately.

      **[!] RETRACTION of my own conclusion two entries above.** The K1n A/B concluded "the packed
      gather and packed store are BOTH EXONERATED" because all three arms failed at the same
      magnitude. That inference was **invalid**: all three were dominated by the page-stride bug,
      which made them equal regardless of their differences. Once it was fixed, the same A/B
      separated cleanly -- G=1 passes, G=4 fails -- and the packed path *was* implicated after
      all. Comparing arms that share a dominant fault measures the fault, not the difference. This
      is [[gate-needs-noise-floor-and-reference]] again: the A/B had no validated reference arm,
      and a PASS somewhere in the matrix is what would have shown the comparison was live.

      Also fixed, latent: both terminal returns in `UnifiedWgmmaTileScheduler` were still
      **positional** -- 13 and 14 values into a 15-field `WorkTileInfo`, so `counter` received
      `ptr_begin`, `ptr_begin` received `ptr_end`, and `num_kv_chunks` received `counter+1`. The
      comment in `load()` documents exactly this hazard; the conversion to designated initialisers
      had been applied to `load()` only. Not the cause of any measured symptom here.

      **[x] K1n RESOLVED for the single-tile FA3 arm (2026-10-10): FA3 PASSES, rel 0.002292,
      0/128. Two bugs, both found by parameter A/Bs on one build.**

      | step | fa3_1chunk | fa3 (multi-tile) |
      |---|---|---|
      | before | 11.8, 127/128 | 48.93, 258/258 |
      | + `fa3.k_page_stride` / `v_page_stride` assigned | 1.001, 127/128 | 1.593, 258/258 |
      | + `FLASHINFER_FUSED_FA3_CAUSAL=1` | **0.002292, 0/128 PASS** | 4.856, 258/258 |

      **Bug 1 -- the page stride was never assigned.** `fa3.k_page_stride` / `fa3.v_page_stride`
      were never set and `FA3ParamsSel fa3{}` zero-initialises them. 0.7's `sparse_mainloop`
      computes `my_kv_offset = page_idx * k_page_stride + entry_idx * k_stride_n`, so with the
      page stride at 0 every page resolved to offset 0 and, at `page_size=1` (`entry_idx` always
      0), **every key read page 0**. These are the same fields 0.7 inserted mid-struct; the FA2
      persistent params already set their equivalents, only the FA3 selection block was missed.
      Fifth instance of the family in [[upstream-fa3-subset-params]].

      **Bug 2 -- the CAUSAL default rested on a vacuous measurement.** `FLASHINFER_FUSED_FA3_CAUSAL`
      defaulted to 0 because "CAUSAL=1 is worse" had been measured -- but that was measured *while
      bug 1 was live*, when every key held page 0's data. With all keys identical, causal and
      non-causal are indistinguishable, so the measurement could not have discriminated and
      whichever arm looked worse was noise. The reference is bottom-right causal and the stock
      wrapper is built `causal=True`, so 1 is the only value that makes the comparison mean
      anything. Null case: `FA3_CAUSAL=0` reproduces 1.001 / 127-of-128 exactly on the same build.

      **What this retracts.** The entire "PV accumulator duplicates rows / every output row equals
      reference row 0 / identity matches 1/128" investigation was a *consequence of bug 1*, not a
      finding about the MMA: with every key reading page 0, all rows attend to identical keys and
      every row's output is legitimately V[0] -- which is exactly reference row 0 under
      bottom-right causal. The accumulator was computing correctly on the input it was given. The
      "duplicated Q input" reframing recorded just above is likewise withdrawn: Q was never
      duplicated. `tOrO(0)==tOrO(2)` was real and correctly measured; the inference from it to a
      broken MMA was wrong.

      **What found it.** `KVCONST=1`, which makes every kv page identical so a kernel reading the
      WRONG kv row still gets the RIGHT values. It flipped a 127/128 failure to **PASS at
      2.372e-07**, localising the defect to kv addressing in one run after many turns of probing
      the accumulator. The null case (`KVCONST=0`, rel 11.8) ran first. Stated limit of that
      discriminator, recorded before use: with constant K the softmax weights are uniform, so
      reading too FEW keys also passes -- it isolates addressing, not the iteration count.

      Two hypotheses refuted along the way, both by probes with their expected output stated
      first: (a) `FA3_STAGES=1` collapsing the pipeline -- eliminated, since one q tile against
      one kv tile is a single mainloop iteration with no buffer reuse, so the stage count cannot
      matter for this fixture (and `STAGES=2` still cannot launch: a traits limit); (b) the KV
      gather's shuffle invariant `kv_offset % KV_STRIDE == group_id`, which **holds** -- measured
      `bad=0` over 16 pairs per block, with a positive confirmation line so silence could not be
      mistaken for the probe not running. Dims: CTA_KV=128, NUM_KV_PER_ITER=16, KV_STRIDE=8,
      8 groups x 16 threads, NUM_COPY_THREADS=128.

      not the mainloop. Next, and the same method: an A/B that makes the split not happen

      **[!] REFRAMING (2026-10-10): the accumulator duplication implies DUPLICATED Q INPUT, and
      the gather's SOURCES were only ever verified for row 0.**

      The PV accumulator holding identical values in both rows of its 2x2 fragment is what the MMA
      produces when **fed two identical q rows**. Identical outputs from distinct inputs would be
      a hardware fault; identical outputs from identical inputs is correct behaviour. So the likely
      state is that `sQ` rows are duplicated and the MMA is faithfully computing the same answer
      twice.

      **Two of my own checks fail to exclude that, for the same reason each time:**
      1. The `[qld]` probe printed `src_off` for `pr0 = tile_base` **only** -- row 0 of each tile,
         never `i >= 1`. So the gather's **destinations** are verified (`[cov]`: 128/128 rows
         written, all predicated valid) while its **sources** are verified for one row per tile. A
         gather reading the same Q row for every `i` passes every check I ran.
      2. The `[sqv]` probe I cited as showing "sQ values distinct" read `sQ` with **naive logical
         indices** -- the same pattern that made the `sO` probe misreport a row's elements, and
         which I had to un-retract. Its distinctness claim is unreliable for that same reason.

      **Same failure shape as the store-side bug: destination verified, source not.** There I
      found it by comparing values against **all** reference rows rather than their own expected
      row. The equivalent here: print `src_off` for `i = 0` **and** `i = 1`.

      **Expectation, stated first:** `packed_coord` maps `pr` and `pr+1` to the **same token at
      the next head-in-group**, so `src_off` must differ by exactly one head's stride (128 elements
      at HEAD_DIM=128). **Equal offsets confirm the duplication at its origin.**

      **Stage count: CORRECTED (2026-10-10).** An earlier commit message claimed the stage count
      is pinned at 1 because the fused kernel reserves **both** roles' storage, calling that "a
      real cost of fusion". **Withdrawn.** Making the FA2 reservation conditional on the split
      (`sm_split < nsm`) and running `SM_SPLIT=all FA3_STAGES=2` **still** fails with
      `invalid argument` -- so FA3's **own** two-stage `SharedStorage` exceeds the limit at these
      traits (CTA_Q=128, CTA_KV=128, HEAD_DIM=128), with no FA2 reservation present. **The
      one-stage pipeline is a traits limit, not a fusion cost.** The conditional reservation is
      kept as a tidy-up (drops 69632 B per CTA when the split is all-FA3), not a fix. The
      one-stage hypothesis for the accumulator row collapse is **untestable**, not refuted.

      **Method note:** this A/B was the single most informative run of the item -- one environment
      variable, no code change, four candidates retired at once. Against the many turns spent
      adding probes: changing a parameter and comparing two runs of the **same build** beat

      `convert_type`. Coinciding => the PV MMA or `attention_updater` replicates one row. Not

      **Why this took fifteen turns to see:** every address check verified **destinations**, and

      The stride assumes all `num_threads` (128) participate; the guard admits only the write warp.

      hunk, re-running `port07/tests/nvcc_check.sh` after each.

      **What `cluster_override` and `tid_base` are for, since they are the fused design and not
      incidental:** `cluster_override` lets the fused kernel's dynamic scheduler hand a block a
      cluster index rather than deriving it from `blockIdx` -- that is the mechanism by which an
      SM that finished FA3 picks up FA2 work (cross-role backfill). `tid_base` lets a warpgroup
      compute `ltid = threadIdx.x - tid_base` so FA2's roles address shared memory correctly
      when they occupy only part of a fused block. Neither has a 0.7 equivalent because neither
      exists upstream; they are the fusion.
